ideas.title: A snowball that grows as it rolls
ideas.critique: This round answers the round-1 risk. A PrintSim body whose mass and inertia grow, Bekker sinkage giving the rolling resistance, and IPC deciding whether a stacked head stays put make it an engineered toy rather than a radius counter. The whole idea rests on the ball really changing inertia and wobbling off-centre. If the growth is a scale change on a sphere, the film becomes 'a ball rolls downhill' again, like the sun ball.

ideas.title: Sandcastle against the tide
ideas.critique: Drucker-Prager MPM with cohesion set by saturation is the right published method, and it is a real step past round 1's DEM. A tide slumping a wall into a wet fan is a collapse people watch to the end. The risk is scale and the hand tools: a small MPM box can end up as a grey lump with no castle shape, and the bucket and pat can become stamping a preset tower.

ideas.title: Steer a hot-air balloon by the winds
ideas.critique: A delayed thermal response and wind layers that turn with height make a calm, readable skill, and the letter drop gives it a goal. On film it is one craft drifting with the camera following, close to the flight posts. The pressurised cloth envelope is the part most likely to be cut down to a rigid mesh, and the layered wind will only read if smoke and seeds really show it.

ideas.title: Fell a tree to bridge the stream
ideas.critique: The hinge as a shrinking bending strength that steers the fall is a real mechanism and a good decision for the player. But it is a one-shot event: a tree can only be felled once, and the payoff is a log falling and a friend walking over it. Most likely it shrinks to choosing a fall angle followed by a rigid body tipping over, and the FEM sag will be too small to see.

ideas.title: Burn a picture with a magnifying glass
ideas.critique: A caustic traced through a real lens that heats and chars a plank is exactly where a path tracer beats a game engine, and the board stays as a thing you made. The optics is a second cousin of the camera obscura. The play is slow drawing with a bright dot, and the close film can easily look like a decal brush unless defocus rings and clouds dimming the spot are seen.

ideas.title: A trebuchet from logs
same_form: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
ideas.critique: A jointed multibody whose sling releases at the pin is honest physics, and tinkering then firing is a loop people return to. But a trebuchet flinging pumpkins is the most predictable physics toy there is. The film is one thrown object's arc plus a voxel break the island has already shown, so it reads as a known recipe.
